演奏時將短簫垂直持握，吹口端靠近唇部，以刻口發聲。正面四個指孔由手指按閉，背面一: To play, hold the danso upright with the mouth end near the lips and sound it across the notch. Four fingerholes on the front are closed with the fingers, and one thumbhole at the back is controlled by the thumb. The low register sounds with a steady breath, while the high register needs more breath pressure. A beginner can first practise a steady airstream and covering the holes, then work gradually on moving between high and low.

短簫琴身傳統以竹製成，二十世紀以來亦見塑膠製品。發聲體即笛身本身，未另見簧片或膜: The body of the danso is traditionally of bamboo, and since the twentieth century plastic versions also exist. The flute body itself is the sounding body, and no reed or membrane component is recorded. The source does not state the materials of the notch, the edges of the fingerholes or other parts, so all that can be confirmed is that the body is mainly bamboo or plastic.
短簫的聆聽示範可從韓國民間音樂與室內樂編制入手：它既能獨奏，也主要與其他樂器合奏: As listening examples, the danso can be approached through Korean folk music and chamber ensembles: it is played both as a solo instrument and, more often, with other instruments, which shows its actual place in folk and chamber music; the source names no particular composers or pieces, so the examples stay with ensemble and solo settings.
短簫音色清澈，音域為兩個八度，自低G至高G。其發聲以邊棱氣鳴方式產生，低音以平吹: The danso's timbre is clear, and its range spans two octaves, from low G to high G. It sounds as an edge-blown aerophone: the low notes come with an ordinary breath, and the high notes are obtained by varying the breath pressure. Compared with related instruments, the “short” in the name marks it as the shortest of the vertically blown pipes; another Korean end-blown bamboo flute, the tungso, is longer.
短簫（Danso）是韓國傳統竹製邊棱氣鳴笛，屬無簧笛類，分類編號 421.141: The danso is a traditional Korean bamboo edge-blown flute of the ductless flute class, classification number 421.141.12. It is played vertically, has a notch at the top of the tube, four fingerholes at the front and one thumbhole at the back, and a range of about two octaves from low G to high G; the low notes sound with an ordinary breath, the high ones through changes of breath pressure. It came from the Chinese duanxiao, its name being the transliteration, and is commonly used in Korean folk music; it can be played solo, and is often heard with other instruments in chamber ensembles.
短簫（Danso）為韓國邊棱氣鳴／無簧笛類，傳統用於韓國民間音樂。其形制於十九世: The danso is a Korean edge-blown (ductless) flute used traditionally in Korean folk music. The type was introduced from China in the nineteenth century; the Chinese call it duanxiao, a short form of the xiao, and the Korean name is a transliteration of that. The instrument is traditionally of bamboo, and plastic versions have appeared since the twentieth century. The “short” in the name marks it as the shortest of the end-blown pipes, shorter than tungso, another Korean end-blown bamboo flute.
